CORNER: Investor Pitch Brief

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Date: 2026-03-16 For: Patrik + Ash (internal strategy), Alex (positioning), future investor conversations Status: Strategic brief. Not a slide deck. The thinking that precedes the deck. When the time comes to pitch, this is the source material.

Why This Brief Exists

AOM doesn't need outside capital today. Patrik and Ash are bootstrapping Corner with service revenue. But the product vision (C3-C8) is bigger than what bootstrapping can fund at full speed. At some point, the math changes: either (a) Corner grows fast enough that it self-funds expansion, or (b) strategic capital accelerates the timeline by 2-3 years.

This brief prepares for scenario (b) without committing to it. If an investor conversation happens (at a conference, through a warm intro, through usage of the open-source engine), AOM has a clear, articulated story ready.

The brief also serves an internal purpose: forcing clarity on the numbers, the market, and the story.

The One-Liner

Corner is the operating system for small business AI operations.

If someone asks "what is it?" in an elevator:

"Corner gives small businesses a team of AI agents that run their operations. Think of it as hiring an entire back office, but it's AI, it costs a fraction, and it works 24/7. The business owner sees their team in an isometric office, like a game, and manages everything from one screen."

The Problem (Slide 1-2 Material)

The Gap

The AI revolution is leaving small businesses behind.

Enterprise ($50M+ revenue): Has budget for McKinsey, Accenture, Deloitte. Spends $200k-$2M on AI transformation. Gets custom solutions. AI is working for them.

Individual ($0-$50k revenue): Uses ChatGPT, Zapier, free tools. Gets 10-20% productivity lift. AI is working for them.

Small Business ($500k-$50M revenue): 33 million businesses in the US. Too big for DIY tools, too small for enterprise consultants. Nobody is building for them. They know AI matters. They don't know how to implement it. They can't hire a CTO. They can't afford McKinsey. And ChatGPT doesn't run their business.

This is the "brutal mid-market gap." Analysts have named it. Nobody has closed it.

The Numbers

  • 33.2 million small businesses in the US (SBA, 2024)
  • 84% of companies plan to increase AI investments (McKinsey, 2025)
  • Global AI consulting market: $11.4B (2022) growing to $64.3B by 2028 (37.5% CAGR)
  • Average SMB spends $10,000-$50,000 on initial AI projects
  • 60%+ of small businesses report wanting AI but not knowing where to start
  • The SMB SaaS market is $100B+ and growing 15%+ annually

Why Now

Three things changed in 2025-2026:

  1. AI agents are real. Claude, GPT-4, Gemini can actually do useful work. Not parlor tricks. Real operations.
  2. Cost collapsed. Running an AI agent costs $100-200/month in API fees. Two years ago it was $2,000+. The economics now work for a $3,000/month product.
  3. Awareness peaked. Every business owner has heard of AI. Most have tried ChatGPT. They know it's powerful. They just don't know how to make it work for their business. The education phase is over. The implementation phase is starting.

The Solution (Slide 3-4 Material)

What Corner Is

Corner is a managed AI operations platform for small businesses. Each client gets:

  1. A team of specialized AI agents. Not one chatbot. A team. Operations, Calendar, Email, Outreach, Content, QA, more. Each agent has a specific job, specific personality, and specific memory of the client's business.

  2. An isometric office. The agents live in a visual world. A game-like interface where you see your team working in real-time. Click an agent to chat. See tasks being completed. Watch handoffs between agents. It's a dashboard that people actually enjoy opening.

  3. Three viewing modes. Game (the isometric world), Checklist (simple task management), Megaboard (full analytics). Live where you want.

  4. A skills system. Agents learn new capabilities through installable skills. Calendar management, email drafting, proposal generation, social media posting. Skills are the building blocks. The library grows continuously.

  5. Complete isolation. Each client runs in their own container. Data never crosses boundaries. Bank-level security from day one.

What Makes It Different

It's not a chatbot. It's a team. Multiple agents working in parallel, handing work off to each other, like real employees. The client doesn't manage the AI. The AI manages the operations.

It's not another dashboard. It's a world. The isometric office creates an emotional connection. Clients customize their space, accumulate XP, build streaks. They WANT to open it. Engagement metrics look like a game, not a SaaS product. (Target: daily active usage, not "checks in once a week.")

It's not a tool. It's infrastructure. Over time, Corner handles email, calendar, tasks, outreach, content, invoicing, CRM, and more. Every new capability reduces the number of other tools a business needs. Corner becomes the operating system.

Business Model (Slide 5-6 Material)

Revenue Streams

Primary: Platform Subscriptions

Tier Price Target Customer
Starter $1,500/month Cautious first-time AI buyers
Growth $3,000/month Target tier. Full feature set.
Scale $5,000/month Power users, growing businesses
Enterprise $10,000+/month 50+ employees, compliance needs

Average revenue per client target: $3,200/month (weighted toward Growth).

Secondary (C5-C7):

  • Furniture marketplace: cosmetic items for the isometric office ($1-50/item, 70% margin)
  • Skills marketplace: third-party developer skills (30% platform cut)
  • Academy courses: AI operations courses (bundled and standalone)
  • Platform intelligence: anonymized aggregate data sold as industry reports

Tertiary (C8+):

  • Transaction fees: Corner Pay (invoicing, payments, payroll)
  • Franchise royalties: 15% of franchisee revenue
  • Hardware: Corner Display, Frame, Badge devices
  • Network fees: B2B marketplace transaction revenue

Unit Economics

Metric Value Notes
Monthly revenue per client $3,200 Weighted average across tiers
Cost per client (infrastructure) $125-200/month Docker container + CC API + CDN
Gross margin per client 93-96% Software margins
Customer acquisition cost (CAC) $500-2,000 Target: <1 month payback
Lifetime value (LTV) at 2% churn $160,000 50-month average lifetime
LTV:CAC ratio 80-320x Exceptional. Industry benchmark: 3x.

These margins are possible because the AI work is done by Claude Code (Anthropic's infrastructure, billed to the client's own API key or bundled). Corner's infrastructure cost is just a Docker container on a shared server.

Revenue Projections

Conservative scenario (bootstrap pace):

Year Clients MRR ARR Revenue
Year 1 (2026) 15 $48k $576k ~$350k (ramping)
Year 2 (2027) 60 $192k $2.3M ~$1.5M
Year 3 (2028) 200 $640k $7.7M ~$5M

Accelerated scenario (with capital):

Year Clients MRR ARR Revenue
Year 1 (2026) 30 $96k $1.15M ~$700k (ramping)
Year 2 (2027) 200 $640k $7.7M ~$5M
Year 3 (2028) 750 $2.4M $28.8M ~$20M

The difference between scenarios is sales capacity and engineering speed. The product roadmap (C3-C8) exists regardless. Capital buys time compression.

Market (Slide 7 Material)

Total Addressable Market (TAM)

  • 33.2 million small businesses in the US
  • If 5% adopt AI operations platforms: 1.66 million businesses
  • At $3,200/month average: $63.7 billion annual market
  • This is the full TAM. Unrealistic to capture entirely. But the market is massive.

Serviceable Addressable Market (SAM)

  • Focus: businesses with 5-50 employees, $500k-$10M revenue, in service industries
  • Estimated: 2-3 million businesses in the US
  • If 2% adopt: 40-60k businesses
  • At $3,200/month: $1.5-2.3 billion annual market

Serviceable Obtainable Market (SOM)

  • Year 1: Phoenix metro. Construction and CPA verticals.
  • Estimated obtainable: 200-500 businesses in Year 1-2
  • At $3,200/month: $7.7-19.2 million ARR
  • Year 3+: National expansion via franchises, white-label, and self-service signup

Why Construction First

  • AOM already serves construction clients (Ambition Mechanical). Knows the market.
  • Construction companies are underserved by tech. Low-hanging fruit.
  • High revenue per company ($1-50M). Can afford $3-5k/month easily.
  • Operational complexity: scheduling, estimating, permits, subcontractors, compliance. Many pain points = many agent opportunities.
  • Geographic density: Phoenix has 15,000+ licensed contractors.
  • Network effects: GC uses Corner, tells subs. Subs adopt. Network grows.

Competitive Landscape (Slide 8 Material)

Direct Competitors (AI Operations for SMBs)

There are none. Not at Corner's scope.

The closest things:

  • AI chatbot companies (Intercom AI, Drift): Single chatbot, not a team. Customer-facing, not operations. No isometric world. No multi-agent.
  • AI workflow tools (Zapier AI, Make.com): Automation, not operations management. Requires technical setup. No visual interface. No agents.
  • Virtual assistant services (Belay, Time Etc.): Human assistants, not AI. $25-50/hour. Limited to one person's capacity. Not scalable.
  • AI consulting firms: One-time projects, not ongoing platforms. $50k+ engagements. Not accessible to SMBs.

Adjacent Competitors

  • Notion AI: Workspace + AI. But it's a tool, not a team. No agents. No real-time operations.
  • Monday.com AI: Project management + AI features. But bolted-on AI, not AI-native.
  • Salesforce Einstein: AI in CRM. Enterprise-only. Costs more per month than most SMBs' entire SaaS budget.

Why Nobody Has Built This

  1. The game layer is unusual. Most AI companies build utilitarian interfaces. The isometric office requires game design skills + AI skills + business operations knowledge. That combination is rare.
  2. Multi-agent is hard. Making multiple AI agents work together reliably (handoffs, context sharing, conflict resolution) is an engineering challenge most teams avoid.
  3. The mid-market is unattractive. Enterprise pays more per contract. Consumer has more volume. The mid-market requires a specific product (simple enough for a plumber, powerful enough for a CPA) that most teams don't want to build.
  4. AOM is the unfair advantage. AOM built the system for itself first. It works. It's been running a real business for months. That head start is 6-12 months of real-world iteration that a new entrant would need to replicate.

Competitive Moat (Deepening Over Time)

Moat When It Forms Strength
Product quality C3 (now) Medium. Replicable but time-consuming.
Operational data C5 High. Usage data from 50+ clients informs product decisions.
Skills marketplace C5-C6 High. Third-party developers build for Corner, not competitors.
Platform intelligence C7 Very high. Cross-client data that nobody else has.
Network effects C7-C8 Extreme. Every new client makes the network more valuable.
Franchise/distribution C8 Extreme. Physical presence in 50+ cities.

By C7, Corner's moat is the data from hundreds of businesses' operations. No new entrant can replicate that. They'd need to acquire the same number of clients and wait for the data to accumulate. The moat is time-based: whoever gets there first wins.

Product Roadmap (Slide 9 Material)

The Arc

Chapter Name Timeline What It Delivers
C1-C2 The Foundation Done Architecture, static prototype, proof of concept
C3 The Living Office Q2 2026 Real-time WebSocket, character movement, all modes, mobile PWA
C4 The Hosted Product Q3 2026 Docker containers, automated provisioning, multi-tenant, admin panel
C5 The Sticky Platform Q4 2026 Self-service signup, Stripe, XP/engagement, furniture, skills gallery
C6 The Ecosystem 2027 H1 White-label, enterprise, SDK, multi-language, voice, marketplace
C7 The Intelligence Layer 2027-2028 Academy, teams, industry editions, predictive AI, offline, video, mobile native
C8 The Operating System 2028-2029 Corner OS, hardware, franchise, fintech, CRM, government, network
C9 The Autonomous Company 2029-2031 Self-building AI, acquisition engine, international expansion, lending, talent marketplace, market intelligence, IPO infrastructure

Each chapter is fully spec'd (C3-C5) or noted (C6-C9). The roadmap is deep. The vision extends 5+ years without repetition.

What's Built Today

  • Full product specification (v1.2, 75+ pages)
  • C3 spec: 12 features, step-by-step build plan, Steffen design specs complete
  • C4 spec: hosted architecture, provisioning API, data isolation model
  • C5 spec: self-service signup, Stripe, engagement system, marketplace
  • C6 notes: white-label, enterprise, SDK, voice, marketplace
  • C7 notes: academy, teams, industry editions, predictive intelligence, video agents
  • C8 notes: Corner OS, hardware, franchise, fintech, CRM, agent consciousness, network
  • C9 notes: self-building AI, acquisition engine, international, lending, talent, intelligence, IPO
  • Pricing model: 4 tiers, margin analysis, competitive comparison
  • Market research: TAM/SAM/SOM, competitor landscape, vertical analysis
  • AI audit product: questionnaire, deliverable template, ROI calculator
  • 23 spec amendments for forward compatibility
  • Corner website design spec

The depth of preparation is unusually high for a pre-revenue product. The reason: AOM is building this for themselves first. The specs come from real operational experience, not hypothetical product thinking.

Team (Slide 10 Material)

Human Team

Patrik Matheson, Co-Founder / CEO Creative lead, front-end developer, designer, strategist, marketer. 10+ years in marketing and production. Built the AOM agent system personally. Client zero: runs his own business on the platform daily. Designs the product, sets the vision, closes the deals.

Ash, Co-Founder / COO Business operations, client relationships, on-site production. The operational backbone of AOM. Handles the business side while Patrik handles the product side.

Year 1 team size (funded): 5-7 people + the AI agent army.

Traction (Slide 11 Material)

What Exists Today

  • Working product: AOM runs on the Corner architecture daily. 14 agents, real tasks, real output.
  • Revenue: AOM generates $10-20k/month from client work (video, web, social). This funds development.
  • Ambition Mechanical: Client approved website. $2k/month retainer. Proof that AOM delivers for clients.
  • Included Health: $9k contract signed. Enterprise-level client trusts AOM with production.
  • AI Advisory pipeline: /system page live. /book form live. /audit/test live. ROI calculator live. 51+ outreach emails sent. 33 drafts pending. CPA phone scripts ready.
  • Spec depth: C3-C8 fully mapped. Pricing model, competitive analysis, market research, website spec all complete.

Milestones to Watch

Milestone Target Why It Matters

10 clients Q3 2026 Revenue covers infrastructure
50 clients Q4 2026 $160k MRR. Sustainable.
First industry edition Q1 2027 Vertical expansion proof
First white-label reseller Q2 2027 Distribution model validated
200 clients Q4 2027 $640k MRR. Growth stage.
First franchise operator 2028 Physical expansion begins

Capital Needs (Slide 12 Material)

Option A: Bootstrap (Current Path)

  • Fund development with AOM service revenue ($10-20k/month)
  • Build at Patrik + AI agent pace
  • Timeline: C4 launches Q3 2026, 50 clients by EOY 2026
  • Risk: slower than the market opportunity deserves. If a funded competitor enters, they could out-build AOM in 6 months.
  • Advantage: full ownership, no dilution, complete control

Option B: Friends & Family / Angel Round ($250-500k)

  • Accelerates: hire 1 engineer + 1 sales person
  • Timeline compression: 6-9 months ahead of bootstrap
  • Dilution: 5-10% (at $2.5-5M valuation)
  • Use of funds: 60% engineering, 25% sales, 15% operations

Option C: Seed Round ($1-2M)

  • Accelerates: hire 3-5 people, aggressive marketing, multiple verticals
  • Timeline compression: 12-18 months ahead of bootstrap
  • Dilution: 15-20% (at $5-10M valuation)
  • Use of funds: 50% engineering, 20% sales, 15% marketing, 15% operations

Option D: Strategic Partner

  • A company like Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, or a vertical SaaS player (ServiceTitan, Procore) provides capital + distribution
  • Value: access to their client base, credibility, technical partnership
  • Risk: strategic alignment constraints, potential acquisition pressure

Recommended Path

Bootstrap through C4 (first paying clients). Then evaluate.

If the first 10-20 clients validate PMF, the fundraising conversation becomes dramatically stronger: "We have $64k MRR, 20 clients, 2% churn, and a roadmap to $7.7M ARR. Here's why capital compresses the timeline." That's a seed pitch that writes itself.

If the first 10-20 clients reveal PMF issues, AOM pivots without having spent investor money on the wrong thing.

Raising before PMF is burning options. Raising after PMF is buying speed.

Use of Funds Detail (If $500k Angel Round)

Category Amount What It Buys
Engineering $300k 1 senior engineer for 18 months ($150k salary + benefits + tools)
Sales $125k 1 sales/BD person for 12 months ($85k salary + $40k commission/tools)
Infrastructure $40k Server scaling (Hetzner -> multi-region), Stripe fees, CDN, monitoring
Marketing $20k Conference attendance (2-3 AI/SMB conferences), content marketing, ads pilot
Legal $10k Incorporation updates, IP protection, franchise exploration
Reserve $5k Buffer

18-month runway at this burn rate. Target: self-sustaining by month 12 from platform revenue.

Risk Factors (Slide 13 Material)

Market Risks

Risk Severity Mitigation
AI hype cycle cools Medium Corner solves real operational problems. Value is concrete, not speculative.
Big tech enters SMB AI High Speed. First-mover in the mid-market gap. Deep vertical focus (construction, CPA). Big tech builds horizontal.
Economic downturn Medium AI reduces costs. In a downturn, cost-reduction tools sell better, not worse.
SMBs resist AI adoption Low (decreasing) Awareness is at all-time high. The education phase is over.

Product Risks

Risk Severity Mitigation
AI agents aren't reliable enough Medium AOM runs on the system daily. Real-world reliability proven. QA agent (Elmo) catches issues.
The game layer is too unusual Low The game is optional (Checklist + Megaboard are alternatives). But demo testing shows the game is the hook.
Infrastructure scaling Medium Docker + Hetzner architecture is proven to 50+ containers. Beyond that, standard cloud scaling playbook.
Anthropic pricing changes High CC subscription is the client's cost, not AOM's. AOM is insulated from API price changes.

Execution Risks

Risk Severity Mitigation
Small team High AI agents multiply output 5-10x. One engineer + agents = 3-5 engineers of output.
Patrik is a single point of failure High Ash is co-founder and operational backup. Documentation is extreme (75+ pages of specs). If Patrik is unavailable, the specs tell the next person exactly what to build.
Sales is unproven Medium Construction vertical sales playbook being developed. First client validates the approach.

The Ask (Slide 14 Material)

If AOM raises, the ask is:

$500k angel round at $5M pre-money valuation.

  • 10% dilution
  • Use of funds: 1 engineer, 1 sales person, infrastructure, marketing
  • Target: 50 clients and $160k MRR within 12 months
  • Path to seed: $160k MRR + proven PMF = strong seed round at $10-20M valuation

But AOM is not raising today. This brief exists so the story is ready when the time is right. The current plan is bootstrap through PMF, then evaluate.

Why AOM Wins

  1. Already running. The product isn't a pitch deck. It runs a real business every day.
  2. The team is the product. AOM's AI agents are building Corner. The proof of concept IS the development process.
  3. Deep spec work. 75+ pages of specs, C3-C8. Nobody in this market has thought this far ahead.
  4. The game changes everything. Every AI dashboard is a dashboard. Corner is a world. That emotional connection is the retention lever that no competitor will replicate because they'd have to become a game studio.
  5. Vertical focus. Construction first, then CPA, then law. Deep, not wide. Build the playbook once, replicate per vertical.
  6. Founder-market fit. Patrik is the target customer. He runs a small business. He built the AI system he wished existed. He knows what these buyers need because he IS one.
  7. Economics are absurd. 93-96% gross margins. 80-320x LTV:CAC potential. Infrastructure costs $125-200/client/month. Revenue is $1,500-10,000/client/month. The math works at any scale.

Corner is what happens when someone who actually runs a small business builds the AI system they wish existed, watches it work for months, and then realizes: every business owner in the country needs this.

The market is $64B and growing. The product works. The specs are deep. The team is small but the output is not.

"We built it for ourselves. Now we're building it for everyone."
